per_req.notes: RE-CHECK FOCUS (QB-008 oscillation guard vs unbounded intent): NO HARM. findings.title: Confidence cross-check can critical-HALT a terminal-size committee that FR-FLOW-025 ACs describe as deciding by plurality (defensible safety layer, non-blocking)
findings.description: Introduced/clarified by QB-001/009. FR-FLOW-025 AC-3 says a non-unanimous non-max 5-member committee 'decides by plurality', and AC-4 says the --max 7-member committee decides by plurality 'without requiring unanimity'. The §4.1.2 committee confidence cross-check adds a path where a TERMINAL-size committee (non-max 5 / --max 7) with a highest-lowest confidence spread >= 0.3 does NOT decide by plurality but escalates to critical and HALTs for the user. A strict reading could see this as narrowing FR-FLOW-025's 'auto-decide replaces block'. It is judged NOT a mismatch because: (i) the trigger is a reliability signal (confidence spread), orthogonal to the plurality vote-counting rule the ACs specify — the plurality rule remains the default and is preserved; (ii) the SRS is silent on confidence; (iii) it mirrors the pre-existing §4.1.1 safety pattern (business-decision confidence below threshold -> critical) and the FR-FLOW-025 Implementation Notes guardrail that critical escalations still halt under --auto. Flagged for transparency and for the SRS record.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional (SRS-side, not a skill defect): if the confidence-reliability HALT at terminal committee size should be a governed behavior, add a one-line FR-FLOW-025 AC or Implementation Note acknowledging that a terminal committee may escalate to a user HALT on unreliable confidence rather than always deciding by plurality. No skill change required.
